title: Checked Size Arithmetic
prompt: ISO C. Implement `int alloc_safe(size_t count, size_t elemsz, size_t *out_bytes)` — compute count*elemsz for allocation; on overflow of the multiplication, or count/elemsz 0 (refuse zero-size asks), return -1 and leave *out_bytes alone; else store the product and return 0. (On this platform you may detect overflow via division: count > SIZE_MAX / elemsz.)

tests.name: overflow detected
tests.hint: (size_t)-1 times 2 wraps: the division check catches it and *out_bytes is untouched.

tests.name: zero refuses
tests.hint: Zero-sized allocations are a caller bug: refuse, never hand out a 0-byte pointer to loop over.
